rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO): annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement:
Rent in RSO units may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. The rate was 3% for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

Changes effective February 2, 2026:
- Landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities.
- The extra 10% for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.
- A 10% increase is still allowed for an additional non-dependent tenant if the landlord acts within 60 days of learning of that tenant.

Increases that need LAHD approval:
- Capital Improvement Program (RAC Reg 210).
- Primary Renovation Program (RAC Reg 220).
- Seismic Retrofit Program.
- Rehabilitation Program (RAC Reg 250).
- Just and Reasonable Rent Increase (RAC Reg 240).

Reset to market rate: rent may go to market after a voluntary move-out, an eviction for nonpayment, lease violation, failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan or a City Attorney order, or a Tenant Buyout Agreement.

Surcharges: landlords may pass through, as separate monthly amounts, the RSO registration surcharge ($1.61) and the SCEP surcharge ($2.83). These may be collected only after the landlord registers the units and gives written notice. A $3.00 surcharge is allowed for a hard-wired smoke or combination smoke/CO detector.

Past moratorium: rent increases were prohibited from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.

State law requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.

Also covered: residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks. Condominiums and townhomes are covered, but their rent is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Units under the RSO are excluded from the state AB 1482 cap.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO eviction controls: just causes, notices, Declaration of Intent to Evict and relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed reasons.
- At-fault causes: nonpayment, uncured lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, denial of reasonable access, or an unapproved subtenant.
- No-fault causes: owner or relative move-in; resident manager move-in (only if required by law, an affordable housing covenant or a regulatory agreement); demolition, conversion or permanent removal from the rental market (Ellis Act, LAMC 151.22-151.28); government order to vacate; HUD sale; residential hotel conversion or demolition; and conversion to affordable housing.

Nonpayment: since March 27, 2023, a tenant may not be evicted unless the rent owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.

No-fault eviction steps:
- File a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice.
- Give 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension).
- Pay relocation assistance per unit, split pro rata among tenants, using the higher amount if more than one applies.
- Make the payment available within 15 days of service, or place it in escrow within that period.

Notice filing: every termination notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service (Bulletin A says 3 days).

Reduced 'Mom and Pop' relocation applies only to owner or relative occupancy evictions under LAMC 151.30.

Exceptions to relocation:
- No relocation is owed when replacing one resident manager with another.
- No relocation is owed for natural-disaster hazards not caused by landlord negligence.
- Accumulated rent may be offset against relocation, except for government orders to vacate or unpermitted dwellings.

Right to Counsel: since August 20, 2025, the Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted, given at the start of tenancy, and attached to any eviction notice.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement:
Landlords of JCO units may not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
- At-fault causes: nonpayment, uncured lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar agreement, denial of reasonable access, or an unapproved subtenant. At-fault evictions carry no relocation.
- No-fault causes: owner or immediate family move-in; resident manager move-in when required by law, covenant or regulatory agreement; demolition, permanent removal or conversion to non-residential use; government order to vacate; HUD sale; residential hotel conversion or demolition; and conversion to affordable housing.

No-fault eviction steps:
- File a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice.
- Pay relocation assistance using the same Chart A amounts as the RSO. Make it available within 15 days of service, or place it in escrow.
- For a single-family dwelling owned by a natural person (including via a trust or controlled entity) who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City, relocation is one month's rent, as payment or credit.
- Accumulated rent may be offset, except for government vacate orders or unpermitted dwellings.

Nonpayment: since March 27, 2023, no eviction unless the rent owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent.

Notice filing: all eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.

Registration and posted notices:
- Properties must be registered annually.
- The Notice of Renters' Protections is required for tenancies beginning or renewing on or after January 27, 2023.
- The Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted and given from August 20, 2025.

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO): relocation and occupant protections for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement:
The RPO applies when an owner demolishes a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years after filing a Notice of Intent to Withdraw (RSO units) or a Declaration of Intent to Evict (JCO units).

Relocation:
- The owner must pay the higher of the state Housing Crisis Act amount or the City amount.
- All tenants get at least the RSO/JCO Chart A amounts within 15 days of the termination notice.
- Lower-income households (80% AMI or below) get enhanced relocation.
- The owner chooses one option: Option 1, standardized Chart B payments handled by the City's relocation consultant; Option 2, an approved comparable replacement unit plus Chart A amounts; or Option 3, individualized relocation under an approved plan, plus RSO/JCO amounts within 15 days.

Occupant protections: right to relocation; right to remain up to 6 months before construction, including a 6-month notice to move; right to return if the demolition does not proceed; right of first refusal for some tenants; and tenant notification.

Notice filing: notice copies must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days.

Penalties for non-compliance start at $250,000 per displaced unit, plus withholding of LAHD permit clearances.

rules.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for demolition or conversion to condominiums, cooperatives, hotels or commercial use (LAMC 47.06-47.07)
rules.requirement:
A landlord who demolishes a property, or converts its use to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels or commercial uses, must pay relocation assistance. This applies whether or not the property is subject to the RSO or JCO.

If the City Planning Department has approved a tentative parcel or tract map for a condominium conversion, the tenant may elect to relocate without receiving a termination notice. The landlord must still pay relocation assistance.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement:
Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits. Interest accrues monthly from November 1, 1990, at a rate the City sets annually.
- The accrued interest is paid either as a direct payment or as a credit against rent.
- The landlord chooses the method and must notify the tenant in writing.
- Interest must be paid monthly or yearly. Waiting until the end of the tenancy to pay it does not comply.

This adds to the state deposit cap in Civ. Code § 1950.5 and does not replace it.
